item.title: Economic damage from high energy prices and rising borrowing costs is mounting globally, splitting the world into a new set of winners and losers as countries with limited exposure to the AI boom fall behind

item.title: ECB’s Lane Not Seeing ‘Noticeable’ Pickup in Eurozone Wages
item.content:encoded: Wages aren’t rising at a rate that would trigger inflation alarms, European Central Bank Chief Economist Philip Lane said Thursday.

item.title: Canada Building Permits Rebound in August
item.content:encoded: The total value of building permits rose 8.8% from the month before to a seasonally adjusted 13.57 billion Canadian dollars, the equivalent of $9.55 billion, Statistics Canada said.

item.title: U.S. Import Prices Rose in September
item.content:encoded: Overall U.S. import prices rose 1.1% in September, after expanding by 0.5% in August, the Bureau of Labor Statistics said.

item.title: Canada Housing Starts Rise in September, Though Market Faces Longer-Term Supply Gap
item.content:encoded: Canadian housing starts picked up last month though the pace remains soft as the broader market shows signs of cooling into the end of the year.

item.title: IMF Warns Governments Against Reliance on Short-Term Debt
item.content:encoded: The IMF warned that as inflation shocks become frequent, governments’ shift to selling more short-term debt may have the opposite effect to the one intended.

item.content:encoded: The 1.5% gain over the previous month reflected a plateau in mortgage rates over the summer, but sales activity overall remained subdued.

item.title: Wholesale Inflation Hit Four-Year High in September
item.content:encoded: The producer-price index rose by 1.3% last month, marking the index’s largest advance since March 2022. Economists were expecting a more modest 0.6% increase.
